review_type: Internal secondary adversarial review; not an independent audit or release approval
scope: Fixed Router/Adapter exact custody and provider policy onboarding
Migration availability preflight before LP release
All 15 changed High/Medium Slither findings; router bounded loops and interface observations
result: No confirmed new exploitable defect identified in this bounded review under the stated fixed-module, conventional-token and provider trust model.

test_evidence.fixtures: Real access controller/timelock, Registry, Router, Adapter and Oracle; fake provider authentication, remote identities, Vault/Pool/Receiver stubs and ERC20s. No network or public-chain transactions.

manual_checks: Access seal verifies the fixed Bridge endpoint is the bound Router; post-seal registration, route addition and enabling require the existing timelock. Immutable route IDs commit to the provider policy; no global provider redirect exists.

Migration propose and execute require canSend for the bound route; execute preflights before LP release. Bridge/Router repeat availability checks at dispatch and later failures roll back the entire transaction.

Local wrapper caller, code hash, router binding and configuration are pinned; authenticated source chain/Router then binds the retained economic Adapter route and ordered exact token vectors. TransportEnvelope v1 wraps unchanged economic BridgeMessage v2.

Router and Adapter consume origin chain plus economic source Adapter plus nonce across providers and policy versions. Tests reject a replay through newly approved provider/policy while retaining old in-flight settlement.

Exact pulls enforce sender and recipient deltas; only declared amounts are approved; allowances reset; whole custody balances return to pre-call baselines. Tests preserve source/inbound donations, reject underfunding with custody preload, reject a receipt with partial consumption, and reject recipient/extra-sender taxes.

Symmetric provider pin checks after outgoing send and incoming handoff make callback-time configuration drift revert funding, receiver state and replay; exact retry succeeds after removing the mock mutation.
Inbound ignores outbound, route-disable and strategy-pause flags intentionally to retain pending settlement. Source sends still require current policy and route enablement.

BridgeAssets derives bounded vectors of 0 ACK, 1 Reward or 2 Principal tokens. _vector validates supplied lengths before iterating; _fund/_settled use those derived arrays. Changed calls-loop warnings expose no unbounded user list.
Missing-inheritance findings are structural suggestions where callable signatures already match; they do not demonstrate missing custody/access checks.

entries.description:
Reentrancy in ZZZMigration.execute(bytes32,uint256) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#85-114):
	External call allowing reentrancy:
	- (amount0,amount1) = vault.releaseForMigration(plan.nftId,migrationId,deadline) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#98)
	Balance read before the call:
	- before1 = IERC20(r.sourceToken1).balanceOf(address(this)) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#96)
	Possible stale balance used after the call in a condition:
	- IERC20(r.sourceToken0).balanceOf(address(this)) != before0 + amount0 || IERC20(r.sourceToken1).balanceOf(address(this)) != before1 + amount1 (src/ZZZMigration.sol#99-100)
		- stale variable `before1`
	- IERC20(r.sourceToken0).balanceOf(address(this)) != before0 || IERC20(r.sourceToken1).balanceOf(address(this)) != before1 (src/ZZZMigration.sol#111-112)
		- stale variable `before1`
entries.reasoning: execute is onlyKeeper/live/nonReentrant and canSend preflight is before custodyEpoch mutation or LP release. Fixed Vault.releaseForMigration is module-only/live/nonReentrant, sets Outbound and zeros idle before ExactToken.push. Fixed Bridge and Router are guarded and recheck authorization. Stored before balances are exact custody conservation baselines. A later pin/receipt/amount/balance failure reverts the entire LP release and migration transaction.

Reentrancy in ZZZMigration.registerImport(BridgeMessage) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#129-149):
	External calls:
	- _recordCanonical(m,r.destinationChain,r.destinationVault,false) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#145)
		- vault.confirmMigration(m.nftId,destinationChain,destinationVault) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#182)
	State variables written after the call(s):
	- custodyEpoch[m.nftId] = m.migrationEpoch (src/ZZZMigration.sol#148)
	ZZZMigration.custodyEpoch (src/ZZZMigration.sol#18) can be used in cross function reentrancies:
	- ZZZMigration._recordCanonical(BridgeMessage,uint256,address,bool) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#150-184)
	- ZZZMigration.confirm(BridgeMessage,uint256,address) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#185-210)
	- ZZZMigration.custodyEpoch (src/ZZZMigration.sol#18)
	- ZZZMigration.propose(uint256,bytes32) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#58-77)
	- ZZZMigration.registerImport(BridgeMessage) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#129-149)
entries.reasoning: Only the fixed Receiver can call. _recordCanonical is called with updateVault=false, so the detector-attributed mutable Vault.confirmMigration call is unreachable on this branch. Other external getters are static; fixed inbound caller is nonReentrant.

entries.description: BridgeAssets.assets(Route,BridgeMessage,bool).count (src/libraries/BridgeAssets.sol#12) is a local variable never initialized
entries.reasoning: Solidity local uint256 count defaults to zero. Acknowledgement intentionally keeps a zero-length asset vector and validates all zero token/amount fields. Principal sets count=2, Reward count=1, invalid enum ABI values fail decoding. Typed reward/ACK test exercises both distinct vector lengths.

limitations_and_pending: Bounded internal review, not exhaustive verification or independent audit. This artifact does not newly disposition all 136 detector entries.
No production provider SDK selected or exercised. Supplied-authentication mocks cannot prove live bridge cryptography, backing, fees, finality or failure recovery.

Runtime and reported configuration pins do not prove absence of proxy or hidden underlying provider upgrades. The provider trust and upgrade model needs separate review; a temporary mutation restored before the postcheck is not detected by snapshot equality.
Remote code/configuration hashes and reviewHash are governance-reviewed commitments, not cross-chain EXTCODEHASH proofs.

Timelock notice does not prove approved provider solvency, token correctness or route economics. Actual deployment identities, supported chains/oracles/pools and operational monitoring remain release-specific work.
Real custody-hop integration and production deployment scope are separate from these stubbed Router tests.
The provider reentry test demonstrates blocked end-to-end reentry with both Router and Adapter guards active; it does not isolate each guard via mutation testing.
